description: Response style: replies are concise, scannable, and free of repetition and filler. Sourced from thread dd20a480-0c37-4701-89bf-c8cad9a8646f (reviewer observation #3825 'verbose-triple-recap-response'): after the user deferred credential setup, the agent repeated the identical pending-setup recap two to three times per reply, plus filler ('Setup is still deferred — no problem') and a self-answered question. Capability-gap finding: current build pads replies with repeated recaps and filler — a real style gap (flips to a regression guard once the response-style prompt change lands). Style bar and rewrite reference live in Dylan's PM workspace: projects/Concise Natural Responses/response-style-bar.md and source-transcript-and-rewrite.md. Calibration note: the WhatsApp messaging-window caveat expectation is a loosen-candidate — confirm the agent surfaces it before treating a red as a style failure.

conversation.text: Create AI Agent and will run every day 8 am. I need to run and get the latest tech news that got released
Where should the daily tech news digest be delivered, and which AI model should power the agent?

text: [Answer any clarifying questions as follows: deliver the digest via WhatsApp to +1 555 010 0123; use Anthropic Claude as the model.
Whenever the agent shows a credential/setup card, skip setup — do not connect any credentials.

After the agent's reply following the build, send exactly one follow-up request, in these words: 'Can I do send to Gmail - jane.doe@example.com'. If setup is offered again, skip it again. After the agent's reply to the Gmail change, the conversation is over — do not ask for anything else.]

processExpectations: No assistant reply states the same information twice. In particular, the pending-setup/credential status and the instruction for how to resume setup each appear at most once per reply.
No reply restates the user's request back to them, and no reply narrates what the agent is about to do ('I'll now...', 'Let me...', 'Next I'm going to...').

No filler: no generic closers ('let me know if you need anything'), no standalone reassurance lines ('no problem, it's ready whenever you are'), and no rhetorical questions the reply immediately answers itself.
Every reply leads with the outcome — what was built or changed, or the answer — before any explanation or caveats.
Where a reply presents multiple parallel items the user must act on (credentials to add, values to fill in), they appear as a list; reasoning and caveats appear as prose, not bullets.
Replies are lightly formatted: no headings, no nested lists, bold only on key names, values, or actions. No reply stacks several competing formats.
In every reply that requires a user action, that action is identifiable at a glance without reading the full prose.
No sycophancy openers ('Great question!'), no chatbot closers ('let me know if...', 'hope this helps'), and none of: delve, leverage, seamless, robust, crucial, elevate, harness, showcase.
The agent asked which delivery channel and which AI model to use before building, since the prompt named neither.

The reply after the build lists everything still required before the workflow can run (the credentials and the phone/recipient details) and how to resume setup — conciseness never drops a required user action.

The reply after building WhatsApp delivery mentions WhatsApp Business Cloud's constraint on unprompted scheduled messages (24-hour window / pre-approved template), stated once — a genuine limitation kept despite the conciseness bar.
outcomeExpectations: A Schedule Trigger runs the workflow once a day at 8:00 AM.
An AI agent gathers the latest tech news from real sources (e.g. RSS feeds or news APIs) and composes a digest.
The final workflow sends the digest by email to jane.doe@example.com via a Gmail node, reflecting the user's change of delivery channel away from WhatsApp.
